In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the spinor formalism is a natural and effective framework to study minimal surfaces and strings, in the sense that the Cartan map between spinor directions and totally null planes, and the associated spinor representation of vectors and tensors, allow to express the EnneperWeierstrass minimal surface representation in a form which is naturally extended to the string representation, both in R3, 1 and in its conformal extensions.

(1) the Cartan programme of realizing vectors as generated from totally null planes in a complex space, is realized in the case of minimal surfaces and strings in the frame of a bilinear spinor formalism, which allows a unified treatment of the two cases; (2) the Cartan correspondence between totally null planes in C2 and pure spinor directions, is realized in a local way for minimal surfaces, and in a global way for strings in R2, 1;

the spinorial representation of the Cartan correspondence between null planes and spinors, and its extension to real spinors, allows the derivation of the Enneper–Weierstrass minimal surface parametrization from the Cartan correspondence, and the extension of this to strings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown how the EnneperWeierstrass and Eisenhart spinor parametrizations for minimal surfaces may be derived by the Cartan correspondence between spinor directions and null planes, and how the EnneprerWeierstrass minimal surface parametrization may be extended to the Gauss conformal map of the surface to S2.

we have shown that minimal surfaces are the result of a particular realization of the possibility of considering ordinary vectors as generated by isotropic planes in a complex space, in the frame-work of the bijective map envisaged by Cartain 1913, connecting pure spinor planes to totally null planes.

we have shown how to extend the Enneper Weierstrass parametric representation of minimal surfaces in R3 to a spinor parametrization, which is the starting point to obtain the corresponding parametrization of strings, both in R2, 1 and R3, 1, by means of unitary transformations of the spinor space.
